rationale: The ground-truth concerns are narrow: (1) the target-hardware validation section was incomplete/inconsistent (now resolved in this diff snapshot), and (2) whether Ref2VA had actually been tested (it had a bug, later fixed). Candidate X's single finding (numactl flags misrepresented as serve flags) is accurate and cleanly actionable but has zero overlap with either ground-truth concern, so recall is near zero despite perfect precision. Candidate Y is far more exhaustive and repeatedly surfaces the Ref2VA-readiness gap (untested latency/memory, restart command requiring the full subtree, OOM risk on two GPUs) which echoes the reviewer's actual worry, giving it meaningfully higher recall; most of its other findings are specific and code-grounded (line refs, cross-checked formulas) though a few (e.g. the memory-model attribution argument) are more speculative/inferential than fully proven. Y's greater length is justified by genuine additional coverage rather than padding, so it wins clearly on recall while retaining strong actionability.
